newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: No plan to end SingTel monopoly before 2000-TAS.
newsitem.headline: No plan to end SingTel monopoly before 2000-TAS.

text.p: The Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS) said on Tuesday it did not plan to end Singapore Telecom's (SingTel) monopoly in basic telecommunications services earlier than year 2000.
"There is no plan to bring forward further the expiry of SingTel's monopoly from 2000," Loo Wai Ling, corporate communications executive of TAS told Reuters.
The Business Times on Tuesday said SingTel's monopoly could end sooner than year 2000.
Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan announced in May that Singapore would end SingTel's monopoly on April 1, 2000, seven years before the originally targeted date for deregulation.

On Monday, Singapore was one of four countries to have made improved offers to further liberalise telecommunication services at a sideline meeting at the five-day World Trade Organisation (WTO) conference.
It said details of the improved offer were expected to be announced by Mah on Wednesday.
A ministry official told Reuters that Mah was scheduled to make a speech on Wednesday morning at the WTO. She could not confirm the content of the speech as it was not yet finalised.
